note: Form of government of 196 sovereign states (Wikidata P31 Q3624078), classified by documented rules from Wikidata (P122 basic form of government, P1906 office of head of state, P35/P6 heads, P106 occupation; CC0), the CIA World Factbook 'Government type' (public domain, archive of 2026-09-11) and V-Dem v16 Regimes of the World 2025 (CC BY-SA 4.0; used for rules 3a and 4, so this file is shared under CC BY-SA 4.0). Rules, in order: (1) theocracy if both Wikidata and the Factbook say so; (2) one-party state if a source says one-party or communist state; (3) monarchy if the head of state is a monarch, split into 'monarch rules' when a source says absolute monarchy or V-Dem finds no elected chief executive (closed autocracy), else constitutional; (4) military government if a source names a junta or military council, or V-Dem codes a closed autocracy and the head of state is a military officer who took office in 2019 or later; (5) transitional or other (provisional government, directorial system, 'in transition'); (6) republics by system: Wikidata's term, the Factbook's where Wikidata names none, several or a different one; if neither, presidential when one person is head of state and government. For republics, Wikidata and the Factbook agreed on 65 states; the Factbook decided 65. Formal constitutions and practice differ: a 'presidential republic' may be a dictatorship (see the V-Dem regime layer).
